Benchmark health report

Can this benchmark be trusted to rank models?

A benchmark is a measuring instrument. This report checks the instrument itself: whether its ranking is stable, whether a freshly generated copy gives the same answer, how much the wording of the captions matters, and which tasks and items carry any signal.

Run main · 9 models · 2,520 items · 2,000 bootstrap resamples · analysis seed 20261120

Image suite

6 models, 5 suites generated from seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 72 items per task per suite, 2,160 items in all. Scores use the canonical caption wording unless stated.

Caution

Ranking stability

10 of 15 model pairs are separated by a paired bootstrap on 2,160 items. The top model stays on top in 84% of resamples; the complete order survives in 49%.

Problem

Suite size

Two independent suites of 72 items per task name the same top model 53% of the time, the same top three 53%, and the same complete order 6%.

Caution

Regeneration

Across 5 regenerated suites the overall score moves by 1.68 pp (standard deviation; sampling alone predicts 2.13 pp). 2 of 35 model-task cells differ between seeds more than chance allows. Mean rank agreement between suites: tau 0.73.

Caution

Wording sensitivity

Rewording the captions moves a model's overall score by 2.7 pp on average (largest: 4.4 pp). The median gap between neighbouring models is 1.9 pp. Rank agreement between wordings: tau 0.43.

Caution

Item quality

Of 2,160 items, 103 are answered by no model and 562 by every model, so they cannot separate anyone. 322 items run against overall ability; 367 would do so by chance alone.

Problem

Floor and ceiling

At floor (no model above chance): binding, spatial. At ceiling (every model at or above 95%): object. 3 of 6 tasks can contribute to a ranking.

Caution

Task redundancy

Among informative tasks, the most similar pair is count and digits (Spearman +1.00, 95% interval +0.60 to +1.00). With this few models the interval is wide.

Audio suite

3 models, 3 suites generated from seeds 0, 1, 2, 30 items per task per suite, 360 items in all. Scores use the canonical caption wording unless stated.

Problem

Ranking stability

1 of 3 model pairs are separated by a paired bootstrap on 360 items. The top model stays on top in 56% of resamples; the complete order survives in 56%.

Problem

Suite size

Two independent suites of 30 items per task name the same top model 47% of the time, the same top two 60%, and the same complete order 34%.

Caution

Regeneration

Across 3 regenerated suites the overall score moves by 3.45 pp (standard deviation; sampling alone predicts 4.40 pp). 0 of 12 model-task cells differ between seeds more than chance allows. Mean rank agreement between suites: tau 0.56.

Problem

Wording sensitivity

Rewording the captions moves a model's overall score by 9.4 pp on average (largest: 17.5 pp). The median gap between neighbouring models is 2.9 pp. Rank agreement between wordings: tau -0.33.

Caution

Item quality

Of 360 items, 88 are answered by no model and 53 by every model, so they cannot separate anyone. 100 items run against overall ability; 113 would do so by chance alone.

Problem

Floor and ceiling

At floor (no model above chance): order, tempo. 2 of 4 tasks can contribute to a ranking.

Holds

Task redundancy

Among informative tasks, the most similar pair is bursts and pitch (Spearman +0.50, 95% interval -1.00 to +0.87). With this few models the interval is wide.

Hypotheses written before the run

PredictionOutcome
H1Regenerated suites give the same ranking and scores consistent with sampling noise.partly supported
H2Rewording captions moves scores more than regenerating the items does.failed
H3The effect of wording exceeds the typical gap between neighbouring models.supported
H4At least two image tasks are at floor (spatial and binding expected).supported
H5The control task is at ceiling at its easiest level.supported
H6One suite's worth of items fixes the top of the ranking but not the complete order.partly supported
H7Items in floor tasks do not follow ability; items in informative tasks do.partly supported
H8Accuracy falls with the difficulty level in every task that is not at floor.partly supported
H9At least two audio tasks are at floor (order and tempo expected).supported

How the verdicts are decided

CheckMeasured byHolds ifCaution if
Ranking stabilityShare of model pairs whose paired-bootstrap 95% interval excludes zero.at least 80%at least 50%
Suite sizeAgreement between two suites of the size actually used, resampled independently from the pool.top model 95% and top group 90%top model 80%
RegenerationChi-square test that each model-task accuracy is the same in every seed; rank agreement between seeds.at most 10% of cells rejected and tau at least 0.8at most 10% of cells rejected
Wording sensitivityMean range of the overall score across caption templates, against the median gap between neighbouring models.range no larger than the gapno larger than twice the gap
Item qualityItems with item-ability correlation at or below the threshold, against an exact permutation count; and the share of items that every model answers alike.no more than 1.25 times chance, and at most a quarter of items answered alikeotherwise
Floor and ceilingFloor: no model above chance (exact binomial, Holm-adjusted). Ceiling: every model at 95% or more.no such taskat most a third of tasks
Task redundancyLargest Spearman correlation between two informative tasks.below 0.90.9 or more

Anything short of the caution rule is reported as a problem. The rules are conventions chosen for this report, not established standards.
